title.en: US sailors are said to be jumping off this warship — and Iran is capitalising

summary.en: The ship has set a modern-day record for consecutive number of days at sea.

body.en:
Donald Trump may have several problems in the war against Iran — but a ship ain't one.

Or so the United States president insists, after batting away concerns of difficult conditions on board a long-deployed warship playing a major part in the conflict.

There are growing concerns for the crew members aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, which is currently on a record-breaking nine months at sea. The warship was deployed to the Middle East in January and is supporting US military operations by carrying aircraft and assisting the blockade of Iranian ports .

Without a port call in more than 200 days, it has broken modern US Navy records for consecutive days at sea. Dozens of military families have complained of food shortages, plumbing problems and declining mental health among crew members, with some even telling US media of attempts by loved ones to jump overboard.

Though the vessel is now returning to port, Trump has dismissed concerns about lengthy deployments, saying the ship has been at sea "not nearly long enough".

But as the war shows no signs of ending, his administration is facing not just concerns from military families, but domestic calls for investigations and questions over his military strategy.

There are roughly 5,000 sailors and US Marines on board the vessel, according to US politicians.

Two military-focused outlets, Navy Times and Stars and Stripes, reported sailors were jumping overboard due to burnout and low morale. The outlets spoke to the wives of sailors who had either tried to jump or had witnessed and intervened when others tried to.

In a letter to US defence secretary Pete Hegseth, US Democratic senator Richard Blumenthal described reports of supply shortages, water contamination, plumbing issues, deteriorating mental health, deck safety concerns, and disruptions in the mail system.

Blumenthal also raised concern that extended Navy deployments may be becoming normalised as a "feature rather than an exception" in US military strategy.

But the Trump administration has dismissed media reports as misinformation. Hegseth said reports about conditions on the ship "completely misrepresented" the situation and that the government ensured every ship had "everything" that can be provided at "every single moment".

US Central Command (CENTCOM) said no service members aboard the aircraft carrier have died, but acknowledged one sailor who fell overboard on 3 August "was quickly and safely recovered" — without detailing why the incident occurred.

title.en: Heroes actress Hayden Panettiere dies aged 36
title.zh: 《英雄》女演员海顿·潘妮蒂尔去世，享年 36 岁

summary.en: Panettiere starred in TV shows including Heroes and Nashville along with films Remember the Titans and Raising Helen.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Actress Hayden Panettiere, star of US TV shows Heroes and Nashville, has died aged 36.

"It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of our beloved Hayden. She was an incredible light and a force of nature who brought immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her and to the millions who watched her onscreen," her father, Skip Panettiere, said in a statement reported by US media.

Panettiere played a cheerleader with superpowers in Heroes and had other memorable roles, including in films Remember the Titans and Raising Helen.

Her father Skip Panettiere has asked for privacy "as our family takes time to process this unimaginable loss", in a statement issued through her representative.

Beginning her career as a child actor, Panettiere was just four years old when she was cast on the popular US soap opera One Life to Live.

She later rose to fame playing Claire Bennet in the popular sci-fi series Heroes, which ran from 2006 to 2010.

Panettiere's career spanned three decades with a string of roles in other hit shows and films, including the Scream horror franchise and the romantic comedy I Love You, Beth Cooper.

Earlier this year, she released a memoir titled This Is Me: A Reckoning, recounting the struggles of growing up as a child actor and her experiences with addiction, abuse and later recovery.

In May, Panettiere spoke to the BBC's US partner CBS News about her mother had taken her as an "eight-month-old baby into audition rooms".

"It went from there and progressed into 50 commercials by the time I was five... It just never stopped," she said.

Panettiere is survived by her daughter Kaya with her former partner, Ukrainian boxer Wladimir Klitschko.

In 2015, after giving birth to her daughter, Panettiere revealed she had entered a treatment facility to help with postpartum depression.

"It's something a lot of women experience," she told US talk show Live With Kelly And Michael in 2015.

"You think it's 'I feel negative feelings towards my child, I want to injure or hurt my child.' I've never, ever had those feelings. Some women do.

"It's something that needs to be talked about. Women need to know that they're not alone, and that it does heal."
body.zh: 美国电视剧《英雄》和《纳什维尔》的主演、女演员海顿·潘妮蒂尔去世，享年 36 岁。 她的父亲斯基普·潘妮蒂尔 (Skip Panettiere) 在美国媒体报道的一份声明中表示：“我们怀着深切的悲痛，分享我们深爱的海登的悲惨去世。她是一道不可思议的光芒，是一种自然的力量，给所有认识她的人以及数以百万计在银幕上观看她的人带来了不可估量的爱和欢乐。” 潘妮蒂尔在《英雄》中扮演了一位拥有超能力的拉拉队长，并在电影《记住泰坦》和《抚养海伦》中扮演了其他令人难忘的角色。 她的父亲斯基普·潘妮蒂尔在她的代表发表的一份声明中要求保护隐私，“因为我们的家人需要时间来处理这一难以想象的损失”。 潘妮蒂尔以儿童演员的身份开始了她的职业生涯，当时她才四岁，就出演了美国热门肥皂剧《一生一世》。 后来，她在 2006 年至 2010 年上映的热门科幻连续剧《英雄》中饰演克莱尔·班尼特 (Claire Bennet)，一举成名。 潘妮蒂尔的职业生涯跨越了三十年，在其他热门电视剧和电影中扮演了一系列角色，包括恐怖片《惊声尖叫》系列和浪漫喜剧《我爱你，贝丝·库珀》。 今年早些时候，她出版了一本名为《这就是我：清算》的回忆录，讲述了作为童星成长过程中的挣扎，以及她在成瘾、虐待和后来康复方面的经历。 今年五月，潘妮蒂尔在接受英国广播公司美国合作伙伴哥伦比亚广播公司新闻采访时表示，她的母亲把她当作“八个月大的婴儿带进试镜室”。 “从那时起，到我五岁的时候，它已经发展到了 50 个广告……它就从未停止过，”她说。 潘妮蒂尔身后留下了她的女儿卡亚（Kaya）和她的前搭档乌克兰拳击手弗拉基米尔·克里琴科（Wladimir Klitschko）。 2015年，潘妮蒂尔生下女儿后透露，她已进入一家治疗机构治疗产后抑郁症。 “这是很多女性都经历过的事情，”2015 年她在美国脱口秀节目《Live With Kelly And Michael》中说道。 “你认为这是‘我对我的孩子有负面情绪，我想伤害或伤害我的孩子。’”我从来没有过这样的感觉。有些女人会这样做。 “这是需要讨论的事情。女性需要知道她们并不孤单，而且它确实可以治愈。”

title.en: In pictures: What one of the world's greatest rivers kept hidden — until now

summary.en: The Danube's receding water levels have exposed sandbanks across Europe — and revealed sunken treasures.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及受造之物关怀与环保责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Water levels on the Danube River, the second-longest in Europe, have dropped so low because of drought that the hulks of dozens of World War Two German warships are emerging into view.

They are a curious distraction from the summer heat crisis. The Danube’s record-low water levels have also pushed power plants to the brink of shutting down, and governments across Central and Eastern Europe are taking steps to conserve electricity.

In the middle of the river separating Serbia and Romania near the Serbian port of Prahovo, a rusty hull is now visible along with a broken mast where the Nazi flag used to fly.

The ships, some still laden with weapons, belonged to Nazi Germany’s Black Sea fleet that the Germans deliberately sank as they retreated from Romania and as Soviet forces advanced deeper into Europe near the end of the war.

Historians say up to 200 German warships were scuttled in September 1944 near Prahovo in the Danube gorge as they came under Soviet fire. The idea behind the deliberate sinking was to slow down the Soviet advance in the Balkans. But Nazi Germany surrendered months later, in May 1945.

The sight of the old warships is a reminder that the Serbian government, with European Union financial support, has long been trying to do something about them. Some were removed from the river by Communist Yugoslav authorities, but most have remained because of the explosives they carried.

Now, however, authorities are trying to keep traffic flowing on the Danube, which flows through 10 nations, as the dropping water levels create dangerous conditions. Experts have linked the unusually hot weather to global warming and other factors.

Earlier this month, Romania's army blasted a rock in a branch of the Danube River in an effort to increase the flow of cooling water to the Cernavoda nuclear power plant, where critically low water levels raised the risk of a shutdown.

The Cernavoda plant, which draws all of its cooling water from the Danube, has been threatened by the river's sharply reduced water levels caused by drought.

Also earlier in August, mortal remains of two German Wehrmacht soldiers were exposed by the historically low water level of the Danube near Budapest. A recovery specialist from the German War Graves Commission retrieved the remains from the riverbed in the Hungarian capital.

The team also found two identification tags at the site. According to the association, the bodies were found alongside a German military motorcycle and several anti-tank mines. Consequently, bomb disposal experts were deployed.

title.en: Trump says US to scale back South Korea military drills after it stayed out of Iran war

body.en:
President Donald Trump has said the US will "substantially reduce" joint military exercises with South Korea, citing his "very good relationship" with North Korea's leader Kim Jong Un.

He also noted on Truth Social that South Korea had recently declined to join the US in the "denuclearisation" of Iran.

"These exercises are not only costly, with much of these costs paid for by the United States of America (as usual!), but send a signal that is totally inappropriate and hostile," Trump posted.

Seoul said the drills with the US would proceed "as scheduled". Pyongyang has not yet commented. It comes after North Korea this month conducted ballistic missile tests banned by the United Nations.

Trump said in his social media post on Sunday that it was "too late to cancel", as the US and South Korea were due to start their annual military exercises on Monday.

He added: "While somewhat unrelated (?), I recently asked the President of South Korea if they would like to join us in the Denuclearization of the Islamic Republic of Iran, and they said, 'No thanks!'"

Trump's announcement came less than 24 hours after he posted an old photograph of himself and Kim from 2019, writing the two were great friends "despite the unfriendly look on this particular picture".

Experts suggest the walking back of joint military exercises could carry a high cost with relatively little benefit.

"US-South Korea combined defence exercises are essential for military forces to be ready and capable of doing their jobs," said Leif-Eric Easley, a professor at Ewha University in Seoul.

"Scaling them back can damage alliance coordination, slow the process of South Korea taking on greater responsibility for its own defence, and weaken deterrence against possible conflicts in Asia.

"The cost savings from downsizing drills are marginal, while the diplomatic benefits for relations with North Korea are doubtful."

Last week, US and South Korean military leaders held a joint press conference announcing Ulchi Freedom Shield.

They said the 11-day event would be similar in scale to previous years, with about 18,000 South Korean soldiers participating.

During the news conference, military leaders also mentioned North Korea's deployment of troops to aid Russia's war against Ukraine.

US military spokesperson Ryan Donald said "our training accounts for that threat", referring to North Korean soldiers returning from the battlefield. About 28,500 American military personnel are stationed in South Korea.

On Friday, North Korea's foreign ministry condemned the joint military drills as "a rehearsal for an aggressive war".

The joint exercises come days after South Korea, the US and Japan detected the second North Korean missile test in days.

title.en: Trump envoy Kushner arrives in Israel after rare Hamas talks on Gaza peace plan

summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump's Middle East envoy Jared Kushner has arrived in Israel, where is expected to meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Monday.

It comes after Kushner held rare talks with Hamas to discuss the implementation of the US-backed Gaza peace plan.

Last month, Trump's Board of Peace said it had reached agreement for the "complete disarmament" of Hamas and other armed groups in Gaza. Last week, Israel rejected Trump's 15-point plan, which also calls for Israeli troops to withdraw and for Gaza to be rebuilt under a new civilian Palestinian administration.

Eight Muslim countries issued a statement on Sunday condemning Israel's rejection.

Trump leads the Board of Peace - created as an international organisation originally intended to bring peace to Gaza, but later expanded to include conflicts worldwide.

A Palestinian official told the BBC Trump's son-in-law met a delegation led by Hamas's new leader Khalil al-Hayya in Egypt on Sunday.

Hamas, in a statement, later called on mediators and the Board of Peace to "compel" Israel to approve the roadmap for the next steps.

But Netanyahu faces a tough October election to try to hold onto power, with a coalition that includes ministers in favour of taking a harsher line on Gaza.

Kushner's meeting with Hayya is said to be the first at this level since last year's agreement of a ceasefire for the Gaza Strip.

Board of Peace envoys Nickolay Mladenov and UK ex-Prime Minister Tony Blair were reportedly also part of the meeting - alongside representatives of Egypt, Qatar and Turkey, which have mediated in the peace efforts.

No official statement has been released of the talks reportedly focusing on concrete actions to decommission Hamas's weapons - as well as the withdrawal of Israeli troops and humanitarian efforts.

Whilst in Egypt, Kushner also met Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi. According to Israeli media reports, Mladenov and Blair will also meet Netanyahu on Monday with the aim of advancing Trump's plan.

The Israeli prime minister has said he wants a full Hamas disarmament first in order to implement the deal.

"Israel rejects the Board of Peace's 15-point document on Gaza. The IDF will not carry out any withdrawal until Hamas is genuinely disarmed," Netanyahu said last week, defying Israel's closest ally.

Netanyahu faces pressure within his own cabinet to continue operations in Gaza. Earlier this month, far-right Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir dismissed the draft as "not acceptable".

title.en: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo becomes deadliest in its history
title.zh: 刚果民主共和国爆发埃博拉疫情，成为历史上最致命的一次

summary.en: The outbreak was already the fastest growing on record, caused by a rare species of Ebola called Bundibugyo.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及受造之物关怀与环保责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is now the deadliest in its history, according to public health officials.

A total of 2,325 people have been killed by the virus since it was declared on 15 May, surpassing the death toll of the country's 2018-2020 outbreak.

The outbreak was already the fastest growing on record, UN humanitarian chief Tom Fletcher said last week, warning that "the epidemic is killing someone every 30 minutes".

There is currently no approved vaccine available for the Bundibugyo species that has caused the current epidemic but several are in development, including one based on technology used to develop the AstraZeneca Covid-19 vaccine.

DR Congo's Institute of Public Health on Sunday said it had recorded 4,945 confirmed cases, including 101 in the previous 24 hours.

Comparatively few cases have been identified outside the country: as of 12 August, 20 cases were confirmed in neighbouring Uganda, while two people were treated in Germany and one case was declared in France.

However, the pace of the virus's transmission in Dr Congo, where it has spread to six of 26 provinces, has been described as "exceptional" by the World Health Organization.

According to Reuters, it took close to five months for the world's deadliest outbreak of 2014-2016 in West Africa to reach 1,000 fatalities - the current outbreak reached 2,000 deaths in less than three months.

The outbreak is the 17th to have emerged in DR Congo since Ebola was discovered 50 years ago. Years of conflict and a highly mobile population have added to the country's challenges in controlling the spread of the disease.

The WHO has said it hopes to reverse the spread of the disease within three months but warned that this meant bringing transmission under control and not ending the outbreak entirely.

Ebola is a rare but deadly viral disease and the Bundibugyo species is even rarer, with only two known prior outbreaks.

Symptoms of Ebola, which are similar to the flu or malaria, include fever, headache and tiredness, and can begin suddenly within two to 21 days of infection.

As the disease progresses, vomiting and diarrhoea can develop, leading to organ failure. Contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit causes the virus to spread.

The UK's medicines regulator, the MHRA, has given permission for the first human trials of a vaccine for Bundibugyo to go ahead.

The jab is being created by a team from the University of Oxford based on the same technology used in the Oxford-AstraZeneca Covid vaccine. Three other groups are also developing different vaccines for Bundibugyo.

The WHO is also sponsoring a separate clinical trial in DR Congo to see whether two existing antiviral therapies can improve survival rates.
body.zh: 据公共卫生官员称，刚果民主共和国爆发的埃博拉疫情目前是该国历史上最致命的一次。 自5月15日宣布以来，已有2,325人死于该病毒，超过了该国2018-2020年疫情爆发的死亡人数。 联合国人道主义事务负责人汤姆·弗莱彻上周表示，疫情已经是有记录以来增长最快的一次，并警告说“这种流行病每 30 分钟就有一人死亡”。 目前还没有批准用于引起当前流行病的 Bundibugyo 物种的疫苗，但有几种疫苗正在开发中，其中包括一种基于用于开发阿斯利康 Covid-19 疫苗的技术的疫苗。 刚果民主共和国公共卫生研究所周日表示，已记录了 4,945 例确诊病例，其中 101 例是在过去 24 小时内确诊的。 国外发现的病例相对较少：截至 8 月 12 日，邻国乌干达确诊了 20 例，德国有 2 人接受治疗，法国通报了 1 例。 然而，病毒在刚果民主共和国的传播速度被世界卫生组织描述为“异常”，该病毒已传播到该国 26 个省中的 6 个省。 据路透社报道，西非2014-2016年全球最致命的疫情爆发用了近5个月的时间才达到1000人死亡，而当前的疫情在不到三个月的时间里就达到了2000人死亡。 这是自 50 年前发现埃博拉病毒以来，刚果民主共和国爆发的第 17 次疫情。多年的冲突和人口的高度流动增加了该国控制疾病传播的挑战。 世界卫生组织表示，希望在三个月内扭转疾病的传播，但警告说，这意味着控制传播，而不是完全结束疫情。 埃博拉病毒是一种罕见但致命的病毒性疾病，而本迪布焦物种则更为罕见，此前仅已知爆发过两次。 埃博拉病毒的症状与流感或疟疾类似，包括发烧、头痛和疲倦，并且可能在感染后 2 至 21 天内突然出现。 随着疾病的进展，可能会出现呕吐和腹泻，导致器官衰竭。接触血液或呕吐物等受感染的体液会导致病毒传播。 英国药品监管机构 MHRA 已批准开展 Bundibugyo 疫苗的首次人体试验。 该疫苗是由牛津大学的一个团队基于牛津-阿斯利康新冠疫苗中使用的相同技术研制的。其他三个小组也在为 Bundibugyo 开发不同的疫苗。 世界卫生组织还在刚果民主共和国赞助一项单独的临床试验，看看两种现有的抗病毒疗法是否可以提高生存率。

title.en: Record rains drench South Korean city as landslide kills one

summary.en: It comes as large swathes of East and South East Asia have been pummelled by dats of heavy rain.

body.en:
Torrential rains have pummelled South Korea's Gyeongsang province, triggering a landslide that killed one person and wounded two others.

The landslide buried the first floor of an apartment building in the south-eastern city of Geoje on Monday morning. Rescuers pulled out three people, one of whom was later declared dead, local media report.

This comes as record rainfall triggered by back-to-back storms caused widespread flooding and landslides in parts of China, Japan and the Philippines.

Geoje city saw 124.5mm of rain in a one-hour period, the highest since South Korea's meteorological agency started keeping records for the city in 1972.

Videos on social media show cars submerged in Geoje as strong currents swept the streets.

City authorities announced that some tourist attractions will be closed on Monday due to the heavy rain.

Bus operations and household waste collection have also been suspended due to flooded or damaged roads, authorities said.

On Sunday, authorities urged residents to avoid driving, stay away from places like riverbanks and evacuate to safe areas if needed.

Multiple storms swept through large swathes of East and South East Asia this month, causing widespread flooding and damage to infrastructure.

Forecasters said this year's typhoon season was shaping up to be more intense than usual, due to a strong El Niño that began in June. El Niño pushes up global temperatures and increases the strength of typhoons.

Late last week, "unprecedented" rainfall battered Japan's Chiba prefecture near Tokyo, leaving 10 people dead and stranding thousands at Narita Airport.

On Sunday, Japanese authorities said the 10th fatality was a man in his 30s who was found dead at his home from carbon monoxide poisoning. He had been using a generator due to the power outage, public broadcaster NHK reported.

summary.en: Donald Trump's envoy, Jared Kushner, met with a Hamas leader to advance a peace plan for Gaza. The proposal includes Hamas disarming and Israeli troops withdrawing from the territory.

body.en:
United States President Donald Trump's son-in-law and envoy Jared Kushner met Hamas' new leader in Egypt overnight in a push to revive a Gaza peace plan rejected by Israel.

Two weeks after Hamas endorsed the latest stage of Trump's Gaza plan by saying it would hand over weapons to a new governing committee, Kushner pressed for verifiable disarmament, a key demand of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Netanyahu rejected the Gaza peace plan on 9 August, saying Trump's latest roadmap for peace was "unacceptable".

Hamas chief Khalil al-Hayya took part in the discussions in the Egyptian Mediterranean city of El-Alamein, making his first trip since assuming leadership of the group in July .

In talks with Kushner, Hamas again voiced its commitment to the plan, a source familiar with the talks told Agence France-Presse.

The group said afterwards that it had called on mediators and Trump's so-called Board of Peace to "compel" Israel to "approve the roadmap ... and begin establishing a timetable for its implementation".

A picture released by host Egypt did not include al-Hayya, but showed Kushner at a table alongside members of the Board of Peace, including former United Kingdom prime minister Tony Blair. Qatar and Türkiye, key mediators alongside Egypt, also joined.

For years, the US refused contact with Hamas, but the Trump administration has increasingly been comfortable with direct contact in hopes of ending the devastating conflict, negotiating the October ceasefire agreement.

On Monday, Kushner will see Netanyahu, a longtime hawk who faces a tough re-election fight in October.

The three regional mediator countries and five other countries — Jordan, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Pakistan and Indonesia — condemned Israel's rejection of the plan on Sunday.

In a joint statement, they said "Israel bears direct and full responsibility" for obstructing peace, adding that its refusal "directly threatens to derail extensive efforts" by Trump.

In response, Netanyahu's Likud Party charged that "the Arab countries want to bring down the prime minister" in the election.

The inclusion of the United Arab Emirates is significant as it normalised relations with Israel five years ago.

Netanyahu expressed opposition to the US plan even after he was assured by Nickolay Mladenov, the Board of Peace's high representative for Gaza, that Israel would not need to pull troops out of the war-battered territory until complete disarmament by Hamas.

The board had initially said Israel would start a phased withdrawal in tandem with Hamas' disarmament.

body.en:

Thirty years after the United States artist, considered one of the most influential rappers of all time, was gunned down in a drive-by shooting in Las Vegas, the unsolved killing could finally be brought closer to an answer.

Duane "Keffe D" Davis , 63, is standing trial in Las Vegas, accused of orchestrating the killing and providing the gun used in the shooting.

He has pleaded not guilty to murder, with jury selection underway and opening statements expected this week.

But whether the jury returns a guilty verdict or not, the trial is about more than just a cold case murder.

Known for hits like California Love and the top-selling record All Eyez on Me, Shakur was already one of the biggest stars in hip-hop when he was killed at just 25.

Like other young artists whose lives were cut short, his unresolved murder transformed him into a global cultural icon, with his life and death continually revisited and theorised decades after his death.

Cathy Scott, then a crime reporter with the Las Vegas Sun, remembers the night Shakur was shot on 7 September 1996 well. She had been tipped off by a homicide detective about the shooting.

"He said, 'Get out of bed and go down to the Las Vegas Strip … a rapper by the name Tupac Shakur was shot,'" the author and journalist tells SBS News.

Shakur was in the passenger seat of a BMW, driven by music executive Marion "Suge" Knight, when a white Cadillac pulled up next to them at a red light and opened fire.

Scott says police were initially reluctant to share information about their investigation, with one detective telling her they were concerned the suspected gang-related killing was bad for tourism.

"I really think they thought it would go away," Scott, who later wrote a book about the murder, says.

"The less the police department talked about it, and were open about it to reporters, the more reporters covered it."

The murder came amid a bitter rivalry between the East and West Coast hip-hop scenes.

Shakur had signed with Los Angeles-based Death Row Records, co-founded by Knight and then one of hip-hop's most powerful labels. Shakur's rival, fellow rap star Christopher Wallace, known as The Notorious B.I.G. or Biggie Smalls, was signed to Sean "Diddy" Combs' New York-based Bad Boy Records, Death Row's chief rival.

title.en: UAE, Saudi Arabia, others condemn Israel's rejection of Trump Gaza plan
title.zh: 阿联酋、沙特阿拉伯等国谴责以色列拒绝特朗普加沙计划

summary.en: Several nations, including the UAE and Saudi Arabia, have condemned Israel's rejection of a Gaza peace plan proposed by the Trump administration. This condemnation occurred while US envoy Jared Kushner and Gaza peace envoy Nickolay Mladenov were engaged in ceasefire and implementation talks with regional mediators and...
summary.zh: 包括阿联酋和沙特阿拉伯在内的几个国家谴责以色列拒绝了特朗普政府提出的加沙和平计划。这一谴责发生之际，美国特使贾里德·库什纳和加沙和平特使尼古拉·姆拉德诺夫正在埃及与地区调解员及哈马斯举行停火和执行会谈。

body.en:
The statement came as US envoy Jared Kushner and Gaza peace envoy Nickolay Mladenov held ceasefire and implementation talks with regional mediators and Hamas in Egypt.

The United Arab Emirates and seven other countries on Sunday condemned Israel's rejection of President Donald Trump's plan to end the war in the  Gaza Strip .

It comes a week after Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu rejected the 15-point plan for Gaza, stating that no military pullout will happen until Hamas is "genuinely" disarmed.

Trump's Board of Peace said last month that it had reached a deal for the complete disarmament of Hamas and other armed groups in Gaza.

The foreign ministers of the UAE, Qatar, Jordan, Indonesia, Pakistan, Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Egypt issued their joint statement as Trump's envoy and son-in-law, Jared Kushner, and Nickolay Mladenov, Trump's Board of Peace envoy for Gaza, were in Egypt for Gaza ceasefire-related talks.

Trump announced last month that there had been a breakthrough on a 15-point road map aimed at ending the war in the Gaza Strip.

The plan drawn up by his Board of Peace calls for Israeli troops to withdraw as Hamas gives up its weapons. An international stabilization force would then work alongside a new Palestinian police force to secure Gaza.

"Rejecting the Road Map constitutes an explicit refusal to proceed with the implementation of the Comprehensive Plan, and directly threatens to derail the extensive efforts exerted by US President Trump to bring an end to the war in Gaza and establish the conditions for lasting peace," the foreign ministers said in their Sunday statement.

"Such rejection confirms that Israel now bears responsibility for obstructing the efforts to bring peace in Gaza and the rest of the Occupied Palestinian Territory," they added.

They called on the Board of Peace and the US "to take immediate and concrete measures within its mandate to uphold the integrity of the Comprehensive Plan and prevent any party from obstructing its implementation."

Kushner met Hamas chief, Khalil al-Hayya, on Sunday according to several news agencies citing unnamed sources. 

Kushner and Mladenov were in Egypt and met with mediators from Egypt, Qatar and Turkey to discuss implementation of the deal.

Hamas on July 30 avoided using the term "disarmament," but said it would hand over its weapons to a new Palestinian governing body that would govern Gaza under the supervision of the Board of Peace.

The group, which is designated as a terrorist organization by several countries and the EU, called on mediators and the Board of Peace to "compel" Israel to approve the road map for next steps.

title.en: Ukraine attacks Wildberries, Russia's biggest online market
title.zh: 乌克兰攻击俄罗斯最大的在线市场Wildberry

summary.en: Since mid-July, Ukraine has been targeting warehouses of Russia's largest online retailer Wildberries almost every day. Ukraine says it's disrupting front-line shipments. But experts say it's disrupting Russia's economy.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.zh: 自7月中旬以来，乌克兰几乎每天都以俄罗斯最大在线零售商Wildberry的仓库为目标。乌克兰表示，前线运输受到干扰。但专家表示，这正在扰乱俄罗斯的经济。 周日早些时候，位于莫斯科以南约 40 公里（25 英里）的波多利斯克镇的俄罗斯最大在线市场 Wildberry 的一个仓库发生火灾。这场火灾是乌克兰无人机夜间大规模袭击造成的，其中大部分无人机被俄罗斯防空系统拦截。 周五，乌克兰袭击了莫斯科北部特维尔的另一个 Wildberry 仓库。前一天，它还纵火焚烧了更东部萨拉瓦特的另一个仓库。 过去几周，大约 20 个 Wildberry 物流中心几乎每天都受到攻击。已确认至少九名员工死亡，数十人受伤，少数仓库已停止运营。 总部位于莫斯科的电子商务咨询公司 Data Insight 估计，Wildberry 已经损失了价值 4800 亿卢布（57 亿美元/49 亿欧元）的商品以及约三分之一的仓库空间。该公司及其卖家的损失估计高达 8000 亿卢布（95 亿美元）。 虽然基辅认为该零售商帮助供应俄罗斯军队，但莫斯科坚称其仅用于民用目的。不管怎样，袭击事件给俄罗斯经济带来了越来越大的压力。 地缘政治咨询公司 Rasmussen Global 首席执行官法布里斯·波蒂尔 (Fabrice Pothier) 告诉德国之声：“我认为（乌克兰）正在寻找一个瓶颈。” “从某种程度上来说，野莓是俄罗斯社会和俄罗斯经济的一个瓶颈。” 2022年俄罗斯全面入侵乌克兰并随后对俄罗斯贸易实施制裁后，亚马逊等许多在线电商平台退出了该地区。作为回应，俄罗斯当局允许所谓的平行进口，实质上是允许俄罗斯公司在未经原始权利人同意的情况下进口商品来规避制裁。 这些公司大幅降低传统价格，使其销量猛增。以 Wildberry 为例，其收入在 2021 年至 2025 年间增长了 7 倍。其竞争对手 Ozon 也提供了类似的惊人数字，据报道收入为 4,930 万美元，2025 年将增长 59%。 如今，Wildberry 已成为该国最大的电子商务平台，控制着该国约一半的市场。 Ozon 占据约 30% 的市场份额。它们处理的商品和服务合计相当于俄罗斯国内生产总值 (GDP) 的 8.5% 左右。 继 7 月中旬的最初袭击之后，乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基 (Volodymyr Zelenskyy) 辩称，这些仓库......

title.en: Bus crash in Hungary kills at least 12
title.zh: 匈牙利巴士坠毁，至少12人死亡

summary.en: Police have arrested the driver of a bus that crashed in Hungary, killing at least 12 people. Reports indicated the bus was carrying Polish pilgrims.
summary.zh: 警方表示，一辆在匈牙利坠毁的巴士司机已被逮捕，事故造成至少12人死亡。据报道，该巴士载有波兰朝圣者。

body.en:
Police say they have arrested the driver of a bus that crashed in Hungary, killing at least 12 people. The bus was carrying Polish pilgrims, media report.

At least 12 people have died after a Polish coach crashed into a ditch and overturned in eastern Hungary , police said on Sunday.

According to emergency services, 47 people were injured in the incident, 10 seriously.

The accident occurred on the M3 motorway near Mezokeresztes, around 140 kilometers (87 miles) east of Budapest, according to police in the district capital, Miskolc. 

Police said they believe the driver fell asleep at the wheel during the overnight journey into Sunday. He was subsequently arrested.

Poland's PAP news agency reported that the bus had been carrying a group of pilgrims from Podkarpackie province in the far southeast of Poland .

The group, said to number 59 people, including two drivers, had been returning from Bosnia-Herzegovina , PAP said. 

Hungary's National Directorate for Disaster Management said that several of the passengers had been trapped under the vehicle when it overturned.

  Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar has voiced his condolences to the families of the crash victims in a Facebook message and thanked emergency and rescue services.

Polish President Karol Nawrocki said he was deeply shaken. "In the face of this unimaginable tragedy, which affects us all, my thoughts and prayers go out to the families and loved ones of the victims," the 43-year-old wrote on X.

title.en: Troops from North Korea to boost Russia's Ukraine forces
title.zh: 朝鲜军队将增援俄罗斯在乌克兰的部队

summary.en: Intelligence agencies report that North Korea is preparing to send up to 50,000 troops to Russia to support its forces in Ukraine. However, military experts express skepticism that this deployment will significantly alter the trajectory of the conflict.
summary.zh: 情报机构报告称，朝鲜正准备向俄罗斯派遣多达5万名士兵，以增援其在乌克兰的部队。然而，军事专家们怀疑此举能否从根本上改变俄罗斯与乌克兰战争的进程。

body.en:
Intelligence agencies report that North Korea is preparing to send up to 50,000 troops to Russia. But military experts doubt this will make a fundamental difference in the course of Russia's war with Ukraine.

In late 2024 , North Korea sent troops to help defend the Kursk region of Russia from Ukraine . International officials estimate that 14,000-15,000 North Korean troops were initially deployed to assist Russia in its war in Ukraine .

Now, Ukrainian and international intelligence agencies suspect that North Korea is planning to send an additional 30,000-50,000 troops to Russia . Ukrainian officials have also stated that North Korean ballistic missiles are being fired from Russia.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has raised concerns that North Korea's improved combat and weapons experience could pose a security threat to Ukraine, as well as the Asia-Pacific region.

Observers have had mixed responses to Zelenskyy's remarks. Oleksandr Kovalenko, a military and political expert at the Ukrainian Center for Security Studies, told DW that new troops from North Korea would likely be used to secure Russia's border territories. Aside from remaining in Kursk, North Korean soldiers could also help secure southwestern Vornezh.

"These forces could free up Russian occupational forces," Kovalenko said. "Russia would then be able to deploy around 15,000 troops to battles along front lines in Vovchansk, Kharkiv, Sumy or even Chernihiv."

Kovalenko does not expect North Korean troops to fight on Ukrainian territory. 

The Russian military analyst Ruslan Leviev agrees. "It's one thing to recapture Russian territory," he told DW, "and an entirely different thing to be present on internationally recognized Ukrainian territory, taking part in a war of aggression."

"Diplomatically speaking," he said, "those are two entirely different concepts."

Leviev said he had not seen concrete evidence of a noteworthy North Korean presence in Russia. He said Moscow had enough troops available without having to draw foreign soldiers into the fight. 

"If you look at the front line, you can see that Russia's forces have been fairly active since mid-July," Leviev said. "That's a clear sign they still have enough forces."

Estimates by the economist Janis Kluge, of the German Institute for International and Security Affairs, back this up. title.en: Lebanon says Israeli strikes kill at least 11​​​ people as hostilities intensify

body.en:
At least 11 people have been killed in Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon, the Lebanese health ministry said, some of the deadliest raids since deals in June eased hostilities between Israel and Hezbollah.

The Israeli military said it struck Hezbollah infrastructure overnight in what it describes as a security zone in southern Lebanon in response to actions against its soldiers there.

Iran-backed Hezbollah said in a statement that the attacks would be "met with what they deserve".

The framework leaves Israeli troops inside occupied southern Lebanon until Hezbollah is disarmed and the Lebanese army takes control, terms the group has rejected as surrender.

Lebanon's official National News Agency said seven people were killed when Israeli warplanes struck a house in the southern village of Ansar, while four others were killed in a strike on the village of Deir El Zahrani.

The seven people killed in Ansar included three children and two women, NNA said, adding that a total of 19 people were wounded in the attacks.

At least 4,300 people have been killed in Lebanon in the latest round of hostilities since 2 March.

NNA also reported other airstrikes across southern Lebanon, including on a strategic area north of the Litani River known as Ali al-Taher hill. One, targeting a valley next to Ansar, was the deepest strike into Lebanon in two months.

The office of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, in a statement on X, accused Hezbollah of violating the ceasefire and attacking Israeli soldiers leading to three injuries.

"The IDF (Israel Defense Forces) responded by striking the Hezbollah terror headquarters which ordered the attack," the statement said. "Only later did the IDF learn that Hezbollah deliberately put civilians in that military compound."

The Israeli military said in a statement it killed Ali Samir Al-Haj Hassan, a commander in Hezbollah's elite Radwan Force unit and others when it struck "a central headquarters of the Radwan Force unit", in Ansar.

"At the time of the strike, Hassan’s family was also present with him inside the military headquarters and, according to the claim, was harmed in the strike," the statement added, emphasising that the family was not the target of the strike.

"The martyrs of the Israeli raid on the village of Ansar are not 'military infrastructure' and the women and children killed in it are not military targets," Lebanon's Prime Minister Nawaf Salam said in a post on X.

body.en: Despite the recent hearings in Congress, we seem to be even further from the goal of understanding Covid-19’s origin’s than we have ever been As a microbiologist and infectious disease clinician, it has been tough to watch the recent devolution of public discourse on Covid-19 origins. It has been especially difficult for me to read the comments of Anthony Fauci about the origins debate in his now-public diary . And it has been painful to watch the televised spectacle hosted by the US senator Rand Paul on 29 July involving a hostile interrogation of Fauci. Despite many early pleas, including my own , for a dispassionate, objective assessment of what we know, don’t know and need to know about Covid-19 origins, we seem to be even further from this goal now than we have ever been – plagued by politicization, polarization and illogical thinking. title.zh: “抖音完全打不开”：台湾模拟互联网中断，以应对中国威胁

summary.en: Taiwan conducted its first internet blackout simulation, prompted by concerns over the security of its undersea cables, which are vital for its digital connectivity. During the exercise in Taipei, air raid sirens sounded, mobile alerts pinged, and police directed people off the streets.
summary.zh: 台湾周四首次进行互联网中断模拟演习，原因是担心作为其“数字生命线”的海底电缆的安全。在台北的演习中，防空警报响起，手机警报提示音不断，警察引导人们离开街道。

body.en: Taiwan practised cutting off internet for the first time amid concerns about the safety of the undersea cables that form its ‘digital lifeline’ In Taipei, the streets swiftly empty as air raid sirens ring out and alerts ping on mobile phones. Police officers usher any stragglers into shelters, leaving the capital suddenly deserted. In cities across Taiwan, these kinds of drills are a fact of life every year , amid the growing threat posed by China across the strait, but this time there is something different. Continue reading...
body.zh: 由于担心构成其“数字生命线”的海底电缆的安全性，台湾周四首次练习切断互联网。在台北，随着空袭警报的响起和手机上的警报声，街道迅速空无一人。警察把掉队的人带进避难所，首都突然变得空无一人。在台湾各城市，随着海峡两岸中国构成的威胁日益加剧，此类演习每年都是家常便饭，但这次有所不同。继续阅读...

reflection.en: Taiwan's simulation of an internet blackout highlights the deep anxieties nations face regarding critical infrastructure and potential threats. In moments of such vulnerability and preparation, the ancient promise of Yahweh reminds us not to fear or be dismayed, for divine presence offers strength and help. This spiritual anchor can guide communities as...
reflection.zh: 台湾模拟互联网中断，凸显了各国在关键基础设施和潜在威胁面前的深层焦虑。在面对这种脆弱和准备的时刻，雅伟的古老应许提醒我们不要惧怕，也不要惊惶，因为神圣的同在提供力量和帮助。这个属灵的锚点可以指引社群应对复杂的挑战并建立韧性。

verse.textEn: So do not fear, for I am with you; do not be dismayed, for I am your God.
verse.textZh: 你不要害怕，因为我与你同在；不要惊惶，因为我是你的神。

title.en: The west turns a blind eye to Xi Jinping’s repressive regime in China | Letters
title.zh: 西方国家对习近平在中国的压制性政权视而不见 | 来信

summary.en: Jennifer Hubbard and other letter writers express concern that Western nations are ignoring China's repressive regime, particularly its 'ethnic unity' law used to suppress minorities. They argue that meaningful international diplomacy is urgently needed to address these human rights issues.
summary.zh: 詹妮弗·哈伯德及其他来信者表示，西方国家对中国压制性政权，特别是其用于压制少数民族的“民族团结”法视而不见。他们认为，急需有意义的国际外交来解决这些人权问题。

body.en: Meaningful diplomacy on an international level is well overdue, writes Jennifer Hubbard . Plus letters from Geoffrey Dixon and Jane Renton In his article on China’s latest tool for suppression of minorities, the “ethnic unity” law, Simon Tisdall seems to take it as read that western governments will continue to pay lip service to notions of human rights in China while pursuing short-term economic goals, ultimately destructive to their own productivity ( President Xi never wastes a good crisis. As Iran, Ukraine and Palestine distract the world, he tightens his grip, 8 August ). This has been the pattern since June 1989, the Tiananmen Square massacre. His faint hope that the young urban Chinese might overturn Xi’s regime is a judgment on the failure of western governments to show any foresight, integrity, effective diplomacy, joined-up thinking or action. They rely on the self-sacrifice of individuals such as Jimmy Lai , Lobga Rangzen and countless – often to us nameless – individuals who put their lives on the line while we wring our hands and weep crocodile tears. Continue reading...
body.zh: 詹妮弗·哈伯德写道，早就应该在国际层面开展有意义的外交。再加上杰弗里·迪克森和简·伦顿的来信。西蒙·蒂斯达尔在其关于中国镇压少数民族的最新工具“民族团结”法的文章中似乎认为，西方政府将继续对中国的人权观念口头上说好，同时追求短期经济目标，最终损害他们自己的生产力（习主席从来不会浪费一场好的危机。随着伊朗、乌克兰和巴勒斯坦分散了世界的注意力，他加强了控制，8月8日）。这就是1989年6月天安门广场屠杀以来的模式。他对中国城市年轻人可能推翻习近平政权的微弱希望是对西方政府未能表现出任何远见、正直、有效外交、联合思维或行动的判断。他们依赖于黎智英（Jimmy Lai）、洛布加·让赞（Lobga Rangzen）等个人的自我牺牲，以及无数（通常对我们来说无名）个人的自我牺牲，他们冒着生命危险，而我们则绞尽脑汁，流下鳄鱼的眼泪。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The call for international diplomacy to address the suppression of minorities echoes the biblical mandate to speak for those who cannot speak for themselves. In a world where powerful voices can overshadow the vulnerable, Yahweh reminds us of our responsibility to advocate for justice and the rights of the destitute. May we seek wisdom and courage to uphold...
reflection.zh: 呼吁国际外交以解决少数民族受压迫的问题，与圣经中为不能为自己说话之人发声的命令不谋而合。在一个强大声音可能掩盖弱势群体的世界里，雅伟提醒我们有责任倡导正义和维护贫困者的权利。愿我们寻求智慧和勇气，维护所有人的尊严，特别是那些声音被压制的人。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: Taiwan says it was hit by ‘abnormal’ AI-assisted cyber-attack
title.zh: 台湾称遭受“异常”人工智能辅助网络攻击

summary.en: Taiwan reported detecting "abnormal" AI-assisted cyber-attacks on government agencies last month, originating from overseas. These attacks represent a new kind of threat, with suspected links to China-based hackers.
summary.zh: 台湾报告称，上个月侦测到来自海外、由人工智能辅助的“异常”网络攻击，目标是政府机构。这些攻击代表了一种新型威胁，据称与中国相关黑客有关。

body.en: Taiwan’s statement comes a day after reports that suspected China-linked hackers had carried out a first-of-a-kind breach Taiwan says it detected AI-assisted cyber-attacks on government agencies that came from overseas last month, a new kind of threat that has been reported as “first-of-a-kind breach”. The Ministry of Digital Affairs (MDA) said its cybersecurity monitoring units ‌detected the “abnormal attack” targeting government agencies, which began on 20 July. The National Institute of Cyber Security issued a series of warning alerts while it investigated. Continue reading...
body.zh: 台湾发表声明的前一天，有报道称疑似与中国有关的黑客实施了史无前例的违规行为。台湾表示，上个月检测到来自海外的针对政府机构的人工智能辅助网络攻击，这是一种新的威胁，被报道为“史无前例的违规行为”。数字事务部 (MDA) 表示，其网络安全监控单位检测到 7 月 20 日开始的针对政府机构的“异常攻击”。美国国家网络安全研究所在调查过程中发布了一系列警告。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The emergence of AI-assisted cyber-attacks highlights the constant need for vigilance in a rapidly changing world. Proverbs 27:12 reminds us that wisdom lies in foreseeing danger and taking appropriate refuge. As technology evolves, so must our discernment and protective measures, trusting Yahweh for guidance.
reflection.zh: 人工智能辅助的网络攻击的出现，凸显了在快速变化的世界中保持警惕的持续必要性。箴言27:12提醒我们，智慧在于预见危险并采取适当的避难措施。随着科技发展，我们的洞察力和保护措施也必须随之进步，信靠雅伟的指引。

verse.textEn: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
verse.textZh: 通达人见祸藏躲；愚蒙人前往受害。

title.en: With Hollywood struggling in China, can the Odyssey draw a crowd?
title.zh: 好莱坞在中国市场举步维艰，《奥德赛》能否吸引观众？

summary.en: Christopher Nolan's summer blockbuster, "The Odyssey" (likely Oppenheimer), is set for release across China's Imax screens. This comes at a time when Western films generally face difficulties in the Chinese market, and the film itself has reportedly overcome significant opposition.
summary.zh: 克里斯托弗·诺兰的夏季大片《奥德赛》（很可能是《奥本海默》）将在中国各地的IMAX影院上映。目前西方电影在中国市场普遍举步维艰，而这部影片据报道也克服了来自世界首富的猛烈攻击。

body.en: Christopher Nolan’s epic will be released on Friday across most of the country’s 800 Imax screens, at a time when western films have been struggling The Odyssey, Christopher Nolan’s summer blockbuster juggernaut, has overcome an onslaught of attacks from the world’s richest man and stared down criticism from a classicist who translated the poem , to become one of the year’s most celebrated and highest-grossing films. But this week, the film faces one of its biggest challenges yet. Continue reading...
body.zh: 克里斯托弗·诺兰的这部史诗巨制将于周五在全国 800 块 Imax 银幕上上映，当时西方电影一直在苦苦挣扎，克里斯托弗·诺兰的夏季大片《奥德赛》克服了来自世界首富的猛烈攻击，也顶住了翻译这首诗的古典学家的批评，成为今年最著名和票房最高的电影之一。但本周，这部电影面临着迄今为止最大的挑战之一。继续阅读...

reflection.en: Launching any major endeavor, like a film in a challenging market, requires immense effort and hope for success. Proverbs 16:3 reminds us to commit our work to Yahweh, trusting that He will establish our plans. Even when facing significant headwinds, we can find peace in knowing that our diligent efforts are seen and can be blessed.
reflection.zh: 在充满挑战的市场中推出一部电影这样的大型项目，需要付出巨大的努力并寄予成功的希望。箴言16:3提醒我们，要将我们的工作交托给雅伟，相信他会成就我们的计划。即使面对重重阻力，我们也能在知道自己的辛勤努力被看见并蒙福时找到平安。

verse.textEn: Commit to Yahweh whatever you do, and he will establish your plans.
verse.textZh: 你所做的，要交托雅伟，你所谋的，就必成立。

title.en: Zhu Rongji obituary
title.zh: 朱镕基讣告

summary.en: Zhu Rongji, the fifth premier of the People’s Republic of China, has passed away at 97. He was widely recognized as an economic reformer who famously declared China 'the factory of the world' and was regarded as one of the country's most effective administrators.
summary.zh: 中华人民共和国第五任总理朱镕基逝世，享年97岁。他被广泛认为是经济改革家，曾宣布中国成为‘世界工厂’，并被视为该国最有效的管理者之一。

body.en: Premier of the People’s Republic of China regarded as an economic reformer who declared that the country had become ‘the factory of the world’ Zhu Rongji, who has died aged 97, was the fifth premier of the People’s Republic of China and one of its most effective administrators and economic reformers following its foundation in 1949. In 1991, Zhu was summoned to Beijing, in the footsteps of the then president and party secretary Jiang Zemin , and in the aftermath of the 1989 uprisings in Beijing and the collapse of the Soviet Union. Continue reading...
body.zh: 中华人民共和国总理被誉为经济改革家，宣称中国已成为“世界工厂”。 朱镕基去世，享年 97 岁。朱镕基是中华人民共和国第五任总理，也是自 1949 年建国以来最有效的管理者和经济改革家之一。1991 年，朱镕基追随时任国家主席兼党委书记江泽民的脚步，在改革开放之后被召唤到北京。 1989年北京起义和苏联解体。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The passing of a leader like Zhu Rongji marks the end of a significant chapter, reflecting a life dedicated to public service and economic reform. His legacy reminds us that every life is a race run, with efforts and impacts that shape the world around us. Yahweh invites us to consider how we too might finish our own race with integrity and purpose.
reflection.zh: 朱镕基这样一位领导人的逝世，标志着一个重要篇章的结束，反映了他一生致力于公共服务和经济改革。他的遗产提醒我们，每个人的一生都是一场赛跑，其努力和影响塑造着我们周围的世界。雅伟邀请我们思考，我们又将如何以正直和目标跑完自己的赛程。

verse.textEn: I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.
verse.textZh: 那美好的仗我已经打过了，当跑的路我已经跑尽了，所信的道我已经守住了。

title.en: Mass evacuations in Beijing as Typhoon Dolphin brings more torrential rain to China
title.zh: 台风海豚带来更多暴雨，北京大规模疏散

summary.en: Forecasters warned the Chinese capital could receive more than one-third of its average annual rainfall over 24 hours Thousands of people have been evacuated from areas at risk of flooding and landslides in Beijing, as the remnants of Typhoon Dolphin continue to bring torrential...
summary.zh: 预报员警告称，中国首都北京在24小时内可能迎来超过年平均降雨量三分之一的降水。随着台风“海豚”的残余继续带来暴雨，北京数千人已从有洪水和山体滑坡风险的地区撤离。

body.en: Forecasters warned the Chinese capital could receive more than one-third of its average annual rainfall over 24 hours Thousands of people have been evacuated from areas at risk of flooding and landslides in Beijing, as the remnants of Typhoon Dolphin continue to bring torrential rain to northern and central China. Forecasters warned on Tuesday that the Chinese capital could receive more than 150mm of rain over the following 24 hours, with some districts forecast to exceed 200mm – more than one-third of Beijing’s average annual rainfall of 528mm. Continue reading...
body.zh: 预报员警告说，中国首都24小时内的降雨量可能会达到年平均降雨量的三分之一以上。随着台风“海豚”的余波继续给中国北部和中部地区带来暴雨，北京有数千人已从面临洪水和山体滑坡风险的地区撤离。预报员周二警告说，未来24小时内，中国首都的降雨量可能超过150毫米，部分地区预计将超过200毫米——超过北京年平均降雨量528毫米的三分之一。继续阅读...

reflection.en: As Beijing faces torrential rains and evacuations, the immediate need for safety and shelter is paramount. In times of natural disaster, we are reminded that Yahweh is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble. Even amidst the chaos, we can find solace and resilience in His unwavering presence.
reflection.zh: 当北京面临暴雨和疏散时，对安全和庇护的即时需求至关重要。在自然灾害面前，我们被提醒雅伟是我们的避难所和力量，是我们在患难中随时的帮助。即使在混乱之中，我们也能在祂坚定不移的同在中找到慰藉和韧性。

verse.textEn: God is our refuge and strength, an ever-present help in trouble.
verse.textZh: 神是我们的避难所，是我们的力量，是我们在患难中随时的帮助。

body.en: Anika Wells confirms clampdown on inducements and inducement advertising. Follow today’s news live Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Hume says housing the ‘best indicator of economic security’ in retirement over super The deputy Liberal leader, Jane Hume says the Coalition will reconsider whether Australians should be able to access more of their superannuation balance early after Pauline Hanson called on Sunday for super rules to be “lightened up a bit” and allow workers to their money in times of crisis. It’s something that we will obviously consider as part of our normal processes, that’s not a policy that’s come to our shadow cabinet yet, but of course, it’s something that we would consider. I do think that superannuation is highly valued by Australians, it’s not something that you need in your working life, it’s something you need in your retired life. If you put the Productivity Commission report into any pub across Australia, people read it from cover to cover, [they] all say the system currently is unfair. We’re paying more for it than we were told it would cost. We’re using scarce income tax dollars to prop up a state that doesn’t need it. This is a deal that doesn’t make any other state worse off, makes sure that there’s the right incentives to deliver productivity and economic growth. And also helps the federal budget bottom line by making sure that we can continue to deliver the royalties and the company tax in particular. WA has a significant resources sector and we need the ability to be able to develop those resources because they lead to national economic growth but also are the national bottom line. We have a pretty significant resource state here in New South Wales too, as does Queensland, as does South Australia. And if the logic that WA is arguing for is to apply across the board, then every other state that’s either developing those resources or looking to are entitled to the same benefit. Continue reading...
body.zh: 阿尼卡·威尔斯 (Anika Wells) 确认将严厉打击诱惑和诱惑广告。关注今日新闻直播 获取我们的突发新闻电子邮件、免费应用程序或每日新闻播客 休姆表示，退休金是“经济安全的最佳指标” 自由党副党魁简·休姆 (Jane Hume) 表示，在宝琳·汉森 (Pauline Hanson) 周日呼吁“放宽一点”退休金规则并允许工人在危机时期获得自己的钱后，联盟党将重新考虑澳大利亚人是否应该能够尽早获得更多的退休金余额。显然，我们会考虑将其视为正常流程的一部分，这还不是我们影子内阁的政策，但当然，这是我们会考虑的事情。我确实认为澳大利亚人非常重视退休金，它不是你工作生活中需要的东西，而是你退休生活中需要的东西。如果你把生产力委员会的报告放在澳大利亚各地的任何一家酒吧里，人们都会从头到尾地读它，[他们]都说目前的制度是不公平的。我们为此付出的代价比我们被告知的要高。我们正在用稀缺的所得税来支撑一个不需要它的国家。这项协议不会让任何其他州的情况变得更糟，并确保有适当的激励措施来提高生产力和经济增长。通过确保我们能够继续缴纳特许权使用费，特别是公司税，也有助于联邦预算底线。西澳拥有重要的资源部门，我们需要有能力开发这些资源，因为它们会带来国家经济增长，也是国家的底线。新南威尔士州、昆士兰州和南澳大利亚州也拥有相当重要的资源状况。如果西澳所主张的逻辑是全面适用，那么所有其他正在开发或寻求这些资源的州都有权获得同样的好处。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story draws attention to creation care and environmental responsibility. Genesis 2:15 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with faithful stewardship of creation, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到受造之物关怀与环保责任。Genesis 2:15提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以对受造之物的忠心管家来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: Yahweh God took the man and put him in the Garden of Eden to work it and take care of it.
verse.textZh: 雅伟神将那人安置在伊甸园，使他修理看守。

summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en: Lawyer for the entertainment industry and AFL figure says his career is ‘destroyed’ following conviction Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Entertainment industry and AFL figure Ralph Carr says he is in “living hell” and has been “destroyed” after being convicted of rape, a Victorian court has heard. Carr was convicted of two counts of rape and one count of sexual assault after a trial in the county court of Victoria last month. Continue reading...

title.en: Why mushroom killer Erin Patterson is returning to court this week
title.zh: 为什么蘑菇杀手艾琳帕特森本周重返法庭

summary.en: The 51-year-old is serving a life sentence after she was found guilty of fatally poisoning three relatives at a family lunch.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Erin Patterson, dubbed 'the mushroom killer' after a sensational case, will return to court this week in a bid to overturn her murder convictions for deliberately poisoning three relatives.

Patterson, 51, was last year jailed for life with a non-parole period of 33 years after she was found guilty of murdering her estranged husband's parents, Don and Gail Patterson, both 70, and Gail's sister, Heather Wilkinson, 66.

She killed them by lacing beef Wellington with lethal death cap mushrooms at a family lunch at her Leongatha home in Gippsland, Victoria, in July 2023.

Patterson was also found guilty of attempting to murder Heather's husband Ian Wilkinson, who became gravely ill but survived.

Patterson argued the deaths were a tragic accident, claiming the poisonous fungi were unintentionally included in the meal, and she later covered up her actions in a panic.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The case garnered unprecedented public and media attention and was the subject of several books, television shows and podcasts.

Patterson will face a two-day hearing that starts on Wednesday at Victoria's Court of Appeal in Melbourne's CBD.

The hearing is an application for leave to appeal, which is a formal request to the court to hear the appeal.

The prosecution and defence will submit written and oral arguments, before a full panel of three judges will determine whether the case has merit for an appeal.

If Patterson is successful, the court could quash her convictions and order a retrial, or acquit her.

If the court rules against her, her convictions will stand, and she will serve out the remainder of her sentence.

In that instance, she could appeal to the High Court, which is Australia's highest court and can overturn decisions made in lower courts.

The Director of Public Prosecutions is also appealing the length of the sentence, arguing Patterson — who will be 82 years old when she is eligible for parole in 2056 — should be locked up for life.

If they are successful, Patterson could be re-sentenced to life without parole or a non-parole period of greater than 33 years.

Patterson is not expected to attend the hearing in person, instead appearing via video link from prison.

In documents lodged with the court last year, Patterson, who has always maintained her innocence, argued she suffered a "miscarriage of justice" during the 10-week trial, laying out seven grounds of appeal.

She claimed the prosecution's five-day cross-examination of her was "unfair and oppressive", while the prosecution's closing address "caused a substantial miscarriage of justice".

body.en:
A coalition of rights groups is pleading with the federal government not to revoke work rights for asylum seekers, warning it could expose people to illegal employment conditions and cash-in-hand jobs.

Under pressure on migration policy, the Albanese government is reportedly considering removing work rights for temporary migrants applying for protection visas.

The move has not been formally announced, but the ABC reported the plan was due to be announced earlier this month in a since-cancelled speech by Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke, as part of a move to reduce migration numbers by cracking down on temporary visas and the number of overseas arrivals.

Sources told the ABC discussions within the federal cabinet centred on dealing with people who overstayed their visas, often on bridging visas.

The reports have alarmed community, charity, multicultural and migrant organisations, with over 160 writing to Prime Minister Anthony Albanese warning it would push people to poverty and exploitation, potentially resorting to cash-in-hand employment to make ends meet.

This would then make them "more vulnerable to wage theft, unsafe working conditions, exploitation and abuse. This is fundamentally at odds with Labor’s values," the joint letter, which includes prominent groups like Anglicare Australia, GetUp, Human Rights Law Centre and Multicultural Australia, reads.

The organisations warned that their charities would be forced to shoulder the burden of support at a time when they're already over-stretched.

They said most asylum seekers are unable to access Centrelink and revoking work rights would have "profound" consequences.

"For many people, the right to work is therefore the difference between being able to support themselves and being unable to pay for food, rent, and other essentials."

The organisations acknowledged lengthy wait times in processing asylum and protection claims in the system, but proposed a number of alternatives as a solution, including investing money in ensuring applications are properly assessed by Home Affairs initially, and review tribunals are properly resourced, so that asylum seekers have a "fair chance" to make their case.

"We recognise that Australia's protection system is facing serious backlogs. Those delays undermine confidence in the system and cause real harm and distress to people who can spend years living with uncertainty, waiting for a final decision. We all have an interest in a protection system that is fast, fair and effective."

title.en: Walter led a campaign that resulted in the shutdown of a music venue. He says whingeing is a right

Aussies have long held a narrative of the resilient “battler”. But recent history suggests the days of "she'll be right," may be behind us. Insight explores whether the little Aussie battler still exists or whether a culture of complaint has taken over. Watch Insight episode Wired to Whinge Tuesday 18 August at 8.30PM on SBS or SBS On Demand.

"Whingeing shouldn't be disparaged. I think it's a right in any liberal democracy like Australia," he told Insight.

"There are laws there which have to be upheld; sometimes those laws don't function. People whinge when they don't function."

Having lived in Sydney's Inner west since immigrating from the UK a few years ago, Walter feels a sense of civic duty to the neighbourhood .

He acted on that sense of duty most acutely a few years, taking issue with what he describes as a "problematic nightclub".

"When the club shuts down in the early hours — or late at night, rather — you've got the antisocial aspects of people slamming car doors, people shouting, people urinating in the street, people leaving bottles, cans, et cetera ... "

"People wake up to mess in the morning ... People can't sleep — it stresses people out."

Walter took the neighbourhood's noise complaints, which included a petition signed by more than 150 residents, to the Inner West Council and Liquor & Gaming NSW.

He said there is an "art" to complaining that required one to be organised and to go to the top authorities about the problem.

Alison Flett never imagined her live music venue would cause such conflict when it first opened in 2021.

She had experience running similar venues and made sure every aspect was up to standard.

"It was DA-approved. My lawyers, my town planners, my advisers said, 'You'd be mad not to take this place over'," Alison said.

It was when new government-mandated COVID-19 restrictions — including rules around physical distancing — took effect that she says venues like hers were encouraged to make use of their outdoor spaces.

While this allowed Alison's venue to continue operating, it also meant locals were more exposed to noise; and in 2023, the complaints ramped up.

Alison said one letter from the council even informed her she was on criminal notice.

"I didn't really know what the criminal notice was, because as far as I was concerned, I was just running a live music venue — and that scared me as a young entrepreneurial lady."

title.en: 'Not where the problems are': Working holiday visa slowdown divides parties
title.zh: “问题不在那里”：打工度假签证放缓引发党派分歧

summary.en: Working holidaymakers fill a labour shortage doing jobs like fruit picking, waiting tables and guiding tours in regional areas.
summary.zh: 打工度假者在偏远地区从事采摘水果、服务员和导游等工作，填补了劳动力短缺。

body.en:
The federal government has confirmed it will slow the processing of working holiday visa applications as pressure mounts to reduce net migration numbers. 

Nine newspapers first reported on Saturday that the federal government had paused applications for working holiday visas from 24 countries.

But Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke confirmed on Sunday that working holiday visas were still being processed, but they were being handled "more slowly than they were previously".

However, when asked about the impact of fewer backpackers on the agriculture sector, he pointed to a Pacific workers' scheme as the primary visa for temporary staff.

"One of the things that happened when we started to improve worker protections on (the Pacific scheme) was ... some of the worst operators said, "if we've got to have better standards for (those) workers, we'll just switch to backpackers".

Working holiday visas — often called "backpacker visas" — allow travellers to extend their stay in Australia by undertaking work that addresses labour shortages in Australia — often fruit picking, farm work, mining, or tourism work in regional and remote areas.

The number of working holiday visa holders in Australia passed 210,000 in June 2025, outpacing pre-COVID figures by around 100,000.

The move comes as pressure builds on the Albanese government to bring down net overseas migration, with other parties carving out their migration policy.

Migration experts have warned of the dangers of political parties attempting to blame migrants for a lack of homes , arguing that migrant workforces will be essential to building the required housing stock .

Net overseas migration — a measure covering visitors, family and partner visas, working holidaymakers, skilled migration, and humanitarian intake, alongside returning Australians — fell slightly to 301,000 in 2025, down from 306,000 the year before, according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics.

Labor's long-term target is 225,000 a year over the next three years, though Burke said on Sunday the party's migration policy was still being worked through and needed to go through a full cabinet process.

None of the major parties has yet specified which visa categories they'd cut to hit their targets — though the Coalition has said intake should be tied to housing completions rather than a fixed annual figure.

title.en: Government admits NDIS reforms will impact families, downplays fears over state readiness
title.zh: 政府承认国家残疾保险计划改革将影响家庭，淡化对各州准备情况的担忧

summary.en: The federal disability minister has defended proposed changes to the National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS), acknowledging that the reforms will affect families. The minister also indicated that further amendments are planned to combat fraud and secure parliamentary approval.
summary.zh: 联邦残疾事务部长为国家残疾保险计划（NDIS）的改革措施进行了辩护，承认这些改革将影响到家庭。部长还表示，将进一步修订以打击欺诈行为并争取议会支持。

body.en:
Labor has downplayed concerns that state-based disability supports won't be ready when needed, as the government pushes contentious NDIS reforms targeting fraud and spending through parliament.

A government-led Senate inquiry on Friday recommended National Disability Insurance Scheme changes should be passed with no substantial alterations.

The overhaul would cut a targeted $37.8 billion from the NDIS over four years and remove 160,000 participants by tightening eligibility requirements.

NDIS Minister Jenny McAllister said a deal between the government and the coalition to pass the changes was getting close.

"We're really hopeful and I'd go as far as saying confident that we can reach an agreement," she told ABC's Insiders program on Sunday.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Opposition health spokeswoman Anne Ruston called for a strengthened fraud and corruption response within the disability insurance agency in the inquiry report.

Senator McAllister said the government was still considering evidence brought forward during the inquiry process and flagged fraud as an area to work through with the coalition.

But concerns about the changes remain among advocates — and from at least one state.

In a joint statement, 12 disability advocacy organisations said the reforms should not pass parliament in their current form.

"It must guarantee that people are not diverted from, or lose, NDIS supports unless alternative supports are funded, operational, accessible and available in practice."

Queensland has resisted signing up to the Thriving Kids program, a major plank in federal plans to cut costs from the NDIS.

Under the program, which is due to be rolled out from October, some children aged eight and under with autism or developmental delays would be shifted onto state supports.

Queensland Disability Minister Amanda Camm has refused to back the agreement, labelling the change a cost-shifting exercise that lacked detail.

Despite the conflict, Labor remained confident people with a disability would not be left without the support they needed.

"We don't need to contemplate delay at this point, because we are working with the states and territories toward that January 1 deadline."

Labor's NDIS plan would lead to average funding being cut by about $5000 a year for participants.

"It is a reduction and we don't deny that it will have impacts on people with disability and their families," Senator McAllister said.

She again dismissed calls to introduce an NDIS inspector-general, saying it would risk adding another layer of bureaucracy.

One Nation leader Pauline Hanson has doubled down on notorious decades-old comments criticising Sydney's Mardi Gras, saying she thinks people should keep their sexuality "behind closed doors".

The comments come only days after a colleague declared One Nation "one of the gayest parties in Australia".

In an infamous 1996 interview with 60 Minutes, Hanson responded "I don't like it" while offering her thoughts on the annual LGBTQI+ festival.

"I don't like it because it's promoting something ... that is not natural," she said at the time.

Her "I don't like it" comment was co-opted by musician Simon Hunt, also known as drag queen Pauline Pantsdown, in 1998, and remixed into a parody dance song that made the Triple J Hottest 100 that year.

Three decades later, Hanson said she acknowledged the economic benefit of the pride parade, adding that it was "acceptable" Australia had legalised gay marriage.

"I still don't like the gay Mardi Gras, but that's my opinion," she told News24 on Sunday.

"I think your own personal sexuality should be kept ... behind closed doors. It's no one's business to do it out there with the gay Mardi Gras anywhere.

"I know it brings a lot of tourists to the country. I know it brings a lot of money. I know all this, but that’s my personal opinion. But anyway, good luck to them that they want to do that."

Her comments follow revelations One Nation's candidate for Western Australia's upper house at the 2025 election, Parminder Singh, made several anti-gay comments in a video on social media.

Singh, who was third on One Nation's upper house ticket at the state election, has since been removed from the party's website.

During the week, One Nation MP Barnaby distanced the party from its former candidate's views, describing it as "one of the gayest parties in Australia".

Hanson also rejected Singh's comments, saying she never heard similar views from him when he was a candidate.

The firebrand politician also defended her inability to name the leaders of crucial allies and regional powers when questioned about her foreign policy credentials as a would-be prime minister.

In an earlier interview with News24, the One Nation leader said diplomacy with Australia's neighbours would pose "no problem", despite her notoriously using her maiden speech in 1996 to declare the nation was "in danger of being swamped by Asians".

Asked if she could name the president of Indonesia or the prime minister of Japan, two major regional powers and key Australian trading partners, Hanson said she couldn't.

reflection.en: Public discourse often highlights our differences, yet Yahweh's word reminds us that in Christ, distinctions like gender, race, or social status do not define our worth or unity. This perspective encourages us to see beyond labels and embrace a shared humanity, fostering respect and understanding for all.
reflection.zh: 公共言论常凸显我们的差异，然而雅伟的话语提醒我们，在基督里，性别、种族或社会地位等区别并不定义我们的价值或合一。这种视角鼓励我们超越标签，拥抱共同的人性，培养对所有人的尊重和理解。
